doc.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Gigs he would or would not take: smooth jazz, Ascension, free music, big bands
summary: He would take some smooth jazz and jump at Coltrane's music, but dislikes big bands and would hesitate over Kenny G style or totally free music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Is there a scenario if you could imagine, where you got a phone call to do something that could be a significant musical move and that you would turn down?
Well I won’t say what that was because I turned it down because I didn’t, I mean I didn’t tell them I can’t do it because I don’t like this music, I said I had prior commitments.
In a general sense could you say what kind of things that you wouldn’t go for?

It’s not so easy because it’s really case by case. In other words, I could never say I won’t take a smooth jazz gig because that’s not true, I might. If somebody called me and said look I’m going to pay you some good money, we want you to come out with this funky smooth jazz band, and Eric, you could just play the way you play. You know, you can kind of do what Miles did. You can put a rock beat behind you but you just play the way you want to play on top of it. I’d do that in a heartbeat. If somebody said I want you to come out and I’m going to pay you a lot of money and you have to really try to play like

Kenny G, we really want you to get deep into that style. I’d probably have to say I can’t do that. I don’t think I could. No disrespect to him, I just don’t think I could do that. I think I would be miserable. I mean maybe okay, three or four days and the money is massive, yeah I could go ahead and give it a shot, but that would be a tough one.
What if someone called and said we’re going to do “Ascension?”

Oh I’d love to give that a try, why not, yeah that would be great, I’d love that. Anything that Coltrane every put a stamp on I’d love to give it a try. I don’t know if I could do it. You know if some people said we want to just play absolutely free, there’s no chord, no rhythm, we don’t want to hear one thing that sounds remotely like anything that’s ever been heard before. I might have to really think about that. And certain types of big bands. I know this isn’t necessarily the best thing to put on the record but I don’t necessarily enjoy playing in a big band. I find it really tedious. Probably because I haven’t played in good big bands. I only had a few opportunities and some of them weren’t necessarily that good of an opportunity. But yeah, it’s never been really my cup — I’m more of a small group or medium-sized group guy, that’s more my thing.
